title: The Lilac Photo Collision
skyStory: Fifty-nine percent and fading, the moon is lingering in Aquarius, where it has been running experiments on coincidence. Its latest hypothesis: if two friends watch two lilac bushes long enough, the bushes will start coordinating. Tonight it publishes the results. Mars reads the paper upside down. Saturn peer-reviews it and finds no errors, which is deeply suspicious.

reading: This morning, your lilac watch ends. The bush you've been tracking finally opens, all at once, purple and ridiculous and smelling like every spring at once. You'll take a photo at 8:41 and hit send. Nancy's photo will arrive at 8:41 too. Same minute. Both bushes with one single white blossom tucked among the purple.

DES. Somewhere, the Aquarius moon is high-fiving itself. The rest of the day will run on that strange, fizzy feeling, as if the universe is leaning closer to listen. Use it. Say the encouraging thing you were going to save for later. The [[Three of Cups]] wants friends celebrating together, even across the miles between the cabin and the shore.
joel.mission: Bring one sprig of lilac, or any flower, indoors and put it somewhere you'll pass a dozen times today.
joel.omen: A single white blossom among purple ones. You and Nancy are more in tune than any clock.
joel.elementWhy: lilacs rooted and blooming on cue

reading: The lilac watch reaches its finale this morning, and you'll win, and so will Joel, at the exact same minute. Two photos crossing in the air at 8:41, two bushes blooming on cue, each hiding one rogue white flower like a secret signature.

Don't even scream. Actually, do. The Wood Rat in you will immediately start building theories, and that's half the fun. The other half is simply letting it be magic. Life Path 11 doesn't need an explanation. Spend the afternoon with the window open so the lilac smell can find you. Tell someone the story tonight. Watch them squint, then grin.
nancy.mission: Smell a lilac today, deeply and theatrically, with your eyes closed, as if judging a competition.
nancy.omen: Two of anything, side by side, perfectly matched. The universe is reminding you that you're never solo.
nancy.stoneWhy: a sparkle for a sparkling coincidence

together.text: Two lilac bushes, one minute, one white blossom each. ΔΕΣ, officially. Tonight, each of you set a sprig of lilac beside your stone, the onyx and the ruby, and send a photo. The Aquarius moon has asked for a copy for its records.

game.intro: DES: you both took the same lilac photo. Prove you don't share one brain by being wrong differently.
game.question: What colour are lilacs?
